properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock: Calders Member sedimentary siltstone and sandstone overlain by glacial till. Masonry lithics: Pale buff-grey Craigleith and Hailes sandstone (carboniferous quartz-arenite). Mortar: Traditional hot-mixed hydraulic lime with graded quartz sand. Natural sub-surface drainage toward the Water of Leith basin.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Species: *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime) and *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) within Charlotte Square Gardens. Phenology (late December): Complete winter defoliation, fully exposed ramified branch scaffolding, bare structural silhouettes, and dormant terminal buds.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical public monument and Georgian residential square. Centerpiece: West Register House (former St George's Church, Robert Reid, 1814) featuring a monumental tetrastyle Ionic portico, rusticated podium, square clock tower, and a ribbed circular copper dome on a stepped drum. Flanking: Four-storey Georgian terraced townhouses (Robert Adam design) featuring rusticated ground floors, smooth ashlar upper levels, continuous stringcourses, modillioned cornices, pitched slate roofs with dormers, and regular 6-over-6 timber sash-and-case windows.
